column3: The Hebrew describes the soul as silence toward God; BSB says the soul finds rest in Him.
The Hebrew says not greatly shaken; BSB says never shaken.
The Hebrew addresses all of you as being murdered; BSB asks whether they will throw the man down.
The Hebrew has his mouth in the singular; BSB has their mouths.
The Hebrew has heart in the singular; BSB has hearts.
The Hebrew calls the groups sons of Adam and sons of a man, and compares them with a breath; BSB names lowborn and exalted and calls them a vapor.
The Hebrew says these two things I heard; BSB says I heard this twice.
The Hebrew has his deed in the singular; BSB has his deeds.
